title: Best Freelancer Management System for Growing Operations | Noloco
summary: Compare the best freelancer management systems for permissions, workflows, onboarding, and contractor access.
body_markdown:
Your operations team just brought on a dozen freelancers for next quarter. Payroll can handle paying them. But where do they see their assigned jobs? Where do they upload completed work? And how do you make sure each freelancer only sees the information they actually need?


That’s where a **freelancer management system** comes in.


The right system should do more than handle onboarding, contracts, or payments. It should give freelancers a secure place to access their work, while giving your team control over what they can see and do. And if your business already uses a client portal or internal operations tool, there’s another question worth asking: **do you really need another system just for freelancers?**


## TL;DR


- A freelancer management system should help you onboard freelancers, control their access, and give them a place to actually do their work.
- More than one in four US knowledge workers, 28%, now freelance or work independently, according to Upwork’s 2025 Future Workforce Index.
- Many freelancer management platforms focus primarily on onboarding, classification, compliance, and payments. Depending on your needs, you may still need separate tools for client and internal work.
- With Noloco, freelancers, clients, and internal teams can work in the same system, with role-based permissions controlling what each person can access.
- When comparing freelancer management software, look beyond payments and onboarding. Consider permissions, workflows, integrations, and whether freelancers can work alongside your clients and internal team. ## What is a freelancer management system?


A **freelancer management system** is software that helps businesses manage freelancers and contractors throughout their working relationship.


Depending on the platform, that can include:


- Freelancer onboarding
- Contracts and documentation
- Worker classification
- Payments and invoicing
- Task and project management
- Access permissions
- Forms and file uploads
- Workflow automation
- Reporting and records


The important distinction is between **managing freelancers** and **giving them somewhere to work** .


A freelancer might be onboarded and paid perfectly, but still need to email your team for their next assignment, search through Slack for a document, or log into another project management tool to update a task.


For growing operations, that can quickly become messy.


A useful freelancer management system should connect the administrative side of working with freelancers to the actual work they need to complete.

## Where can dedicated freelancer management platforms fall short?


Dedicated freelancer management platforms can be a strong fit when your biggest challenge is managing contractors at scale, particularly around onboarding, compliance, classification, and payments. But that isn't always the whole problem. For a growing operation, there are two other questions worth considering.


### 1. Where does the actual work happen?


A freelancer might be onboarded in one system, paid through another, and then asked to complete their work somewhere else.


That can mean jumping between your contractor platform, project management software, email, Slack, and a client portal.


When those systems aren't connected, your team ends up spending time moving information between them.


With Noloco,[workflows](https://noloco.io/product/workflows) and[forms](https://noloco.io/product/forms) can sit inside the same interface freelancers use to access their work.


A completed job can trigger the next step. A submitted document can be routed to the right person. A freelancer can update a record without needing your team to copy that information into another system.


### 2. Do you need another system?


A business managing 15–40 freelancers across a handful of projects may have very different needs from a global company managing thousands of contractors across dozens of countries.


Before adding another platform, consider whether you can extend a system you already use to cover freelancer workflows too.


If your client portal, internal tools, and freelancer workflows can all run from the same system, you have fewer places to manage permissions, data, and processes.


## What should you check before choosing a freelancer management system?


Before choosing freelancer management software, ask these questions:


Question to ask Why it matters


Can contractors and clients work within the same permission system? You can manage access centrally instead of maintaining separate systems.


Does it connect to the data you already use? You can avoid unnecessary migration and keep existing data where it is.


Can you control exactly what each contractor can see and do? Contractors should only have access to the records and actions relevant to their work.


Can you track approvals, submissions, and changes? A clear record makes processes easier to manage and review.


Can freelancer workflows live alongside your client portal and internal tools? Keeping related workflows together can reduce the number of systems your team needs to manage.


The best freelancer management system for your business depends on what you actually need to manage.


If your priority is global contractor compliance and payments, look closely at those capabilities.


If your priority is giving freelancers a controlled place to work alongside your clients and internal team, look at permissions, workflows, data connections, and day-to-day usability too.

Dedicated freelancer management platforms can be useful when contractor compliance, classification, and payments are the main challenge. ## FAQ


### What is a freelancer management system?


A freelancer management system is software that helps businesses manage freelancers and contractors throughout their working relationship. Depending on the platform, this can include onboarding, contracts, classification, payments, task management, permissions, workflows, and reporting.


### What's the difference between a freelancer management system and an employer of record (EOR) platform?


An EOR platform, such as Deel, typically focuses on employing or paying workers across countries and handling associated tax and compliance requirements.


A freelancer management system covers a broader range of contractor workflows, which can include onboarding, access management, task or project visibility, and day-to-day work.


### Do I need a dedicated freelancer management system, or can I manage contractors in my existing tools?


It depends on your needs and the number of contractors you work with.


A small number of freelancers can often be managed through existing tools if you have clear processes and permissions. As your contractor workforce grows, a dedicated system or a more structured workflow can make onboarding, access control, and day-to-day management easier to manage.


### What's the risk of not having a system for freelancer access?


Without clear processes and permissions, contractors may end up with access to more information than they need, while your team may struggle to keep track of who has access to what.


There can also be compliance and classification risks. ITV, for example, disclosed £61 million set aside for potential tax liability related to the classification of freelance contributors under UK IR35 rules in its 2024 annual report.


### Can freelancers and clients use the same portal?


Yes. If your system supports role-based permissions, freelancers and clients can use the same portal while seeing different information.


For example, a freelancer could see their assigned jobs and submit completed work, while a client sees their projects and documents. Your internal team can have broader access. See[how the online agency It Just So Happens handles](https://noloco.io/customer-stories/it-just-so-happens-digital-agency) it in the real life.


### Does a freelancer management system replace my project management tool?


Not necessarily.


Some businesses use a dedicated freelancer management platform for onboarding, compliance, and payments while keeping project management elsewhere; while others prefer to bring freelancer workflows into the same system used by their clients and internal team. Which approach makes sense depends on how your operation is structured and what freelancers need to access.
